title: Keep peace alive with Bani
summary: The Perfect Guru gives rare peace by grace, and Bani keeps it sounding. Singing the Word makes forgiveness fruitful instead of fragile.
takeaway: Keep mercy audible by singing the Bani that makes peace fruitful.
lifeApplication: When peace returns, give it a voice before distraction claims it. Sing or recite one line of Bani and let the room learn that sound first.

source.shortMeaning: Peace stays living when the Perfect Guru’s grace is answered by singing Bani.
source.lifeApplication: When relief arrives, speak Bani before noise takes the room back.

evidence.coreClaim: Peace stays living when the Perfect Guru’s grace is answered by singing Bani.
evidence.turn: The shabad names grace as rare and then gives the practice that keeps grace audible — sing Gurbani.
evidence.practicalImplication: When peace returns, give it a voice before distraction claims it. Sing or recite one line of Bani and let the room learn that sound first.
